accompagner-melodie.title: Accompanying a melody
accompagner-melodie.description: Another musician (flute, accordion, trumpet) plays the tune: your job on ukulele is to carry it. Stay steady, change chords with them, and always know where you are in the song.

melodie-01-gaita.title: Listening to the gaita
melodie-01-gaita.description: The gaita is the flute from cumbia's roots. It plays a 4-bar phrase while you play simple strums on the beats. Listen to how the melody "announces" the E7 and then comes back to rest on A minor.
melodie-01-gaita.goal: Change chords together with the phrase, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: First loop: don't play, just listen to the flute and watch the 🎼 lane in "The band".
When the flute drops to G# (G#4), that's the sound of E7: your left hand should already be there.
Play softer than the flute: a good accompanist is heard without covering the melody.
Hum the melody as you play: it's the best way not to get lost.

melodie-02-bolero.title: Bolero: playing softly under a slow melody
melodie-02-bolero.description: A slow trumpet melody with long held notes. The danger: when the melody holds a note, you tend to slow down with it. Your right hand doesn't change: it's what keeps the song moving.
melodie-02-bolero.goal: Stay steady during the held notes, 2 loops at 80 bpm.
tips: The "–" signs on the melody lane are held notes: during them, you're the one keeping the rhythm alive.
Turn the guide down, then off: only your ukulele accompanies the trumpet.
On the G7, the trumpet drops to B (B4): it "calls" you back to C.

melodie-03-couplet-refrain.title: Verse and chorus with accordion
melodie-03-couplet-refrain.description: A real little 8-bar song: a verse in A minor, then a chorus that brightens into C major before coming back. Above the grid, the structure bar tells you where you are and what's coming. The accordion is the sound of Mexican cumbia and vallenato.
melodie-03-couplet-refrain.goal: Go from verse to chorus without getting lost, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Watch the "Verse / Chorus" bar: when it announces the chorus for the next bar, get ready to play a little louder.
The verse goes down toward the low A, the chorus climbs higher: by ear alone, you know where you are without looking.
The E7 at the end of the chorus leads back to the verse: it's the same E7 → Am change as usual.

melodie-04-son-anticipation.title: Son: the trumpet that comes in early
melodie-04-son-anticipation.description: In Cuban music, the melody "anticipates": it hits the next chord's note on the & of 4, half a beat early, then holds it over the bar line. It's unsettling: your right hand has to stay on your pattern, and your chord change stays on the 1.
melodie-04-son-anticipation.goal: Don't change chords early with the trumpet, 2 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: Find the last step of each bar on the 🎼 lane: the note starts there and carries over (–) into the next bar.
You always change chords on the 1. Only the melody is early.
Listen to how it "pulls" the song forward: that's what's called Cuban swing.

melodie-05-morceau-complet.title: The full song: intro, verse, chorus
melodie-05-morceau-complet.description: Ten bars, just like at a real dance: a 2-bar intro where you set up the groove on your own with the band, then the accordion comes in for the verse and chorus. The guide fades away: you're the orchestra's ukulele player.
melodie-05-morceau-complet.goal: Hold the whole song, guide off, 2 loops at 105 bpm.
tips: During the intro, you set the tone: play with confidence, the accordion will lock in with you.
At the end of the intro, the accordion plays two pickup notes (E, D): the verse starts right after.
If you get lost, look at the structure bar and jump back in at the start of the next section.
For an extra challenge: turn on the silence challenge. The melody goes quiet too: you have to find your place in the song.
